state_of_the_art.statement: The integers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are all quadratic residues modulo 1009, so r(2,5,1009) = 1, the smallest start the contract allows, and the optimum is 1. The modulus has 32 runs of five consecutive quadratic residues; the last one starts at 1004.

name: Long intervals containing no modular inverse pair
description: Return [start,length] for a nonempty interval contained in [1,1008]. For EVERY x,y in the interval, including x=y, require x*y %1009 !=1. Maximize interval length. Finite obstruction search for the modular inverse-pair interval question. Diagonal pairs are checked, so the self-inverse residues 1 and 1008 cannot be present; this is stricter than the preliminary distinct-pair proposal.

state_of_the_art.statement: A scan of all intervals in [1,1008] shows that the longest interval containing no x, y (x = y allowed) with x·y ≡ 1 (mod 1009) has length 85: two intervals attain it and none of length 86 exists. Erdős and Graham (1980, p. 89) ask whether every interval of length p^c, c > 1/2, contains such a pair for large p.
